question: By selling an article at (2)/(5) of its actual selling price, Manav incurs a loss of 24%. If he sells it at 88% of its actual selling price, then the profit percentage is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the Actual Selling Price (SP) = 100 units.

Selling at 2/5 means SP = 40 units, which results in a 24% loss (i.e., 76% of CP).

Since 40 units → 76% of CP ⇒ 1 unit → 1.9% of CP.

If sold at 88% of Actual SP, the New SP = 88 units.

Value of 88 units = 88 × 1.9% of CP = 167.2% of CP.

Profit % = 167.2% − 100% = 67.2%.

**∴ The correct answer is 67.2%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling an article at 2/5 of its actual SP causes a 24% loss.

The new selling price is 88% of the actual SP.

**Formula Used:**

SP = CP × (100 − Loss%) ÷ 100

Profit% = [(New SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100
